clue.text: Fish from a rod

definitions.meaning: a freshwater fish with spiny fins
an old unit of length, five and a half yards, also called a pole

explanation.surface: An angler explains where a catch came from: off the end of a rod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' just joins the two senses. The rod here is not fishing tackle but the old British measure of length.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dictionary senses of one word: a common river fish and an old land measure equal to a rod or pole.

clue.text: Work that is blocking the floor

definitions.text: Work that is blocking the floor

parts.words: Work that is blocking the floor
parts.note: reads like an obstruction on the floor, but means a floor laid in wooden blocks

explanation.surface: Building work is getting in the way on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' means laying blocks, not obstructing.
explanation.definitionFit: Inlaid flooring made of small wooden blocks set in a geometric pattern.

clue.text: Vaughan Williams's piece of orchestral phantasy

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A reference to a work from the composer Vaughan Williams's orchestral fantasias.
explanation.walkthrough: The composer's first name is pronounced 'Rafe'.
explanation.definitionFit: The English composer Vaughan Williams had this first name, so the possessive points to him.

clue.text: Main route to Scotland, though it takes longer

definitions.text: Main route to Scotland, though it takes longer

parts.words: Main route to Scotland, though it takes longer
parts.note: alludes to the song Loch Lomond, whose singer taking the low road reaches Scotland before the one on the other way

explanation.surface: Travel advice about the trunk road north.
explanation.walkthrough: In Loch Lomond, 'I'll tak' the low road, and I'll be in Scotland afore ye', so the other road is slower.
explanation.definitionFit: A main road or highway, and the slower route in the Scottish song.

clue.text: One of those heard o'er the lea, example of a small type

parts.words: One of those heard o'er the lea
parts.note: Gray's Elegy has 'The lowing herd winds slowly o'er the lea': one of that herd is a cow, something that lows
a case is an instance or example

explanation.surface: A line about cattle in a pastoral poem drifts into talk of printing type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' puns on the 'herd' of Thomas Gray's famous line; a cow lows, so one of them is a LOWER (rhyming with 'slower').
explanation.definitionFit: Small letters, as opposed to capitals, were kept in the lower tray of a compositor's type cases.

clue.text: Circle Line?

parts.note: looks like the London Underground line, but asks for a line that curves round in a circle

explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; read literally it is any line bent into a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A curve that bends round and closes on itself, as in a noose or ring of string.

clue.text: Lost opportunity with exam questions — scrap the answer

parts.note: a lost opportunity is a waste
an exam paper is the sheet of questions

explanation.surface: A failing student throws the exam away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap the answer' reads as discard what you wrote; 'scrap' is the definition and 'the answer' just points to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded sheets and jottings, the stuff that goes in a bin, are scrap.

clue.text: Expel Bunter's form

definitions.meaning: Billy Bunter, the greedy schoolboy of the Greyfriars stories, was in a class with this name

explanation.surface: A headmaster wants to throw out the fat schoolboy's whole class.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is a comic fat schoolboy in British boys' stories; a form is a school class.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to throw out; some British schools called a class the Remove, as at Greyfriars.

clue.text: Cracked anvil tone of extraordinary volume

indicators.note: something cracked is broken up, so the letters of anvil and tone are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A broken anvil rings out at a startling loudness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' suggests loudness to go with the anvil, but it is a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A work of fiction that rejects conventional plot and character, an unusual sort of book.

clue.text: Characteristic spirit and energy initially needed by Thomas the contractor

indicators.note: needed by means that letter is wanted in front of the next piece
initially means just the opening letter of energy is used

parts.note: Thos is the contracted, shortened written form of the name Thomas

explanation.surface: A builder called Thomas needs spirit and energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contractor' looks like a builder, but it signals the name in contracted form.
explanation.definitionFit: The distinctive character or guiding beliefs of a group or era.

clue.text: π, say, is very exact

definitions.meaning: pi, as in the Greek letter, is also slang shorthand for pious, devout
scrupulous and punctilious, as with devout attention to every detail

explanation.surface: A mathematician praises the precision of the constant pi.
explanation.walkthrough: The symbol suggests the number, but PI is also a colloquial clipping of 'pious', hence devout.
explanation.definitionFit: Pious means devout, and a second sense is scrupulously exact, as in 'with religious care'.

clue.text: Dull cheer-leaders for such a sporting competition!

parts.note: matt or mat means without shine, dull

indicators.note: the leading letters at the front of the word cheer are taken

explanation.surface: Cheerleaders at a game are mocked as rather dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheer-leaders' looks like the pom-pom squad, but it means the leading letters of 'cheer', C and H.
explanation.definitionFit: A game or contest between two sides, as in a football fixture.

clue.text: Sound French article cut

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article, 'a'
to be cut is to be hurt or wounded

explanation.surface: A remark about a French piece of writing being trimmed sounds fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' is an adjective, healthy and undamaged, not a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Safe and sound: uninjured, in one piece.

clue.text: Crumbs! Svengali has gone mad!

indicators.note: something gone mad is crazily jumbled, so the name's letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An exclamation of shock that the hypnotist Svengali has lost his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbs!' reads as a mild oath, but it is the definition, scraps left over. Svengali is the sinister hypnotist of the novel Trilby.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps and remains left after a meal are leftovers, like crumbs on a plate.

clue.text: Foot-long skeleton of Sumatra set in order

indicators.note: putting the letters in order means arranging those of Sumatra set afresh

explanation.surface: A foot-long skeleton found in Sumatra is reassembled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot-long' is not a length: it means the length of bone in the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The group of five long bones in the middle of the foot, between ankle and toes.

clue.text: Describing Pythagorean theorem subsequently in examination

indicators.note: in means the word for subsequently sits inside the word for examination

parts.note: a trial is a test or examination
later means afterwards, subsequently

explanation.surface: Someone will get to Pythagoras later in the maths exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Pythagoras's theorem concerns right-angled triangles, figures with three sides.

clue.text: Hidden underground in case it is blown up

definitions.text: in case it is blown up

parts.note: inner means inside, out of view
the Tube is London's underground railway

explanation.surface: A bomb hidden on the underground railway, in case it explodes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown up' suggests explosions; it means inflated, and 'case' is a tyre's outer cover. The Tube is London's Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The inflatable rubber ring inside a tyre's outer casing, which is pumped full of air.

clue.text: Roman author of "The Full Moon and Sixpence"?

parts.note: a full moon is drawn as a circle, the letter O
six in Roman numerals is VI, and d is the old abbreviation for a penny, so 6d is sixpence

explanation.surface: A spoof of Maugham's novel The Moon and Sixpence credited to a classical writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The title echoes Somerset Maugham's novel. Sixpence was an old British coin, written 6d before decimal currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Publius Ovidius Naso, the Latin poet of the Metamorphoses, wrote in ancient Rome.

clue.text: Hairy, like Byron as acquaintance?

definitions.meaning: Lady Caroline Lamb called Lord Byron 'mad

explanation.surface: A remark that Lord Byron was a shaggy sort to know.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hairy' suggests shaggy, but it is slang for risky. The second sense quotes Lady Caroline Lamb on Byron.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for risky or perilous, and the word Caroline Lamb used for the poet as someone to know.

clue.text: Motorway turning right is hardly the thing

indicators.note: turning means the motorway's name is read the other way round

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI with the figure taken as a letter
proper means right or correct

explanation.surface: A driver doing a right turn on the motorway is behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Yorkshire; reversed, its MI gives IM. 'turning right' looks like a driving move.
explanation.definitionFit: Not done, unseemly: 'not the thing' is an idiom for socially wrong.

clue.text: Statesman's tug

definitions.meaning: read as States man, a man from the United States, an American
a sudden sharp pull, a jerk

explanation.surface: A politician gives something a pull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statesman' suggests a politician; split it as 'States man'. The 's is just 'is' joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for an American, and also a verb meaning to pull sharply.

clue.text: Boat people look inside for a gourd

indicators.note: inside means the word for look is placed within the word for boat people

parts.note: watermen are boatmen who ferry passengers on a river
lo is an old word meaning look, behold

explanation.surface: Refugees at sea search for a gourd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boat people' suggests refugees, but it means river boatmen.
explanation.definitionFit: The large juicy fruit belongs to the gourd family, the cucurbits, with pumpkins and cucumbers.

clue.text: Deliver ransom

definitions.meaning: to save or set free, as in deliver us from evil
to buy back a captive by payment

explanation.surface: An instruction to hand over a ransom.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue or set free, and to buy back by paying, both senses of the same verb.

clue.text: Standard means for churning cheese

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level

indicators.note: churning stirs up the word means so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe line about the usual way of churning cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churning' sits naturally with cheese-making dairy talk, which hides that it is the signal to rearrange; 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard Italian grating cheese from the Parma region.

clue.text: Penny, on the tiles, is tight

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the letter for penny above the next piece

parts.note: the tiles make up a roof

explanation.surface: A cat called Penny out on the tiles is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the tiles' is British slang for out partying, and 'tight' for drunk, but 'tight' here means sealed.
explanation.definitionFit: As a suffix, as in waterproof or soundproof, it means sealed against something, impervious.

clue.text: The captain stands here, where glasses are kep!

definitions.meaning: the raised platform on a ship from which it is commanded
the part of a spectacle frame resting on the nose, keeping the glasses in place

explanation.surface: A ship's captain at the post where the binoculars are stored.
explanation.walkthrough: Glasses suggests a drinks cabinet or binoculars; it is spectacles, which sit on the nose's top.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names the ship's command platform and the piece of a spectacle frame across the nose.

clue.text: The way our brains go empty?

definitions.meaning: the brain ..., the emigration of a country's clever people

explanation.surface: A lament that our minds go blank.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'brain drain' is the loss of a nation's skilled people abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A channel for outflow, as in the brain drain, and the verb to empty out.

clue.text: Measure of the catch for which many dashed

definitions.text: Measure of the catch for which many dashed

parts.words: Measure of the catch for which many dashed
parts.note: a unit for herring catches, the shoals fishing boats raced out to

explanation.surface: Fishermen raced for a catch now measured out.
explanation.walkthrough: A cran is the Scottish measure of fresh herring, the silver darlings that whole fleets dashed out to catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish unit of volume for fresh herring, about 37.5 gallons.

clue.text: Potential seed finds free love around university

indicators.note: around means the reworked letters wrap the letter for university
free means the letters of love are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A student discovers free love on campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' turns LOVE into OVLE, and 'around' puts that round U.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany, the structure in a plant's ovary that becomes a seed once fertilised.

clue.text: Dropping punishment involving an awful jerk

definitions.text: Dropping punishment involving an awful jerk

parts.words: Dropping punishment involving an awful jerk
parts.note: describes an old torture in which a victim was hoisted by a rope and let fall to stop with a violent jerk

explanation.surface: A grim description of an old torture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' tempts as a nasty person, but it is the sudden jolt of the rope at the end of the drop.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic torture: the victim was hauled up on a rope by the wrists and dropped short of the ground.

clue.text: Brother changed forenames

indicators.note: changed means the letters of forenames are reordered

explanation.surface: A monk took a new name on entering the order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brother' suggests a monk or sibling; members of the fraternal order call each other Brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Masonic lodge address one another as Brother.

clue.text: Lets rip in front of society

indicators.note: in front of places the word for rip before the letter for society

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip

explanation.surface: Someone tears their clothes in front of polite society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lets rip' reads as a phrase; 'Lets' is the definition and 'rip' is the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord lets property to tenants, hiring it out for payment.
